Capability: Validates one structured editor-operation intent against a model document, returning findings, diff-preview rows and validation states without mutating or returning a model.
Notes: Native Rust engine reached through a Tauri command and the wasm build; a separate browser-mirror engine outside this area is held to the same shared case corpus.

Capability: Applies one validated editor operation to a cloned model document and returns the new document with a local-session acceptance receipt; blocked operations return no model.
Notes: Receipt records a user-initiated local acceptance basis only; carries explicit no-professional-claim boundary flags.

Capability: Defines the operation-outcome document (diagnostics, diff rows, model-basis hash evidence, validation states, acceptance record) and the supported operation/change-kind taxonomy.
Notes: Unsupported change kinds and operation/change-kind mismatches are blocking findings (OP-KIND-UNSUPPORTED, OP-CHANGE-KIND-MISMATCH).

Capability: Edits single fields of sections, materials, nodes, elements, supports, components, load cases and combinations under per-field rules for text, positive dimensioned quantities and references.
Notes: Component kind and combination term list edits are explicitly deferred and blocked rather than silently accepted; includes material temperature-point shear modulus edits.

Capability: Blocks edits whose stated before-value is stale or whose claimed model hash does not match the current canonical model hash, echoing hash evidence in the outcome.
Notes: Hash computed over RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the whole model document.

Capability: Creates and deletes nodes, refusing deletes of nodes still referenced by pipes, supports, components or loads.
Connects a pipe run between two existing nodes and deletes pipe runs, checking endpoints, section geometry and dependent primitive loads.
Inserts component symbols (bend, tee, reducer, valve, flange, expansion joint) at a node, resolving the required creation geometry and modifiers from explicit input only.
Notes: No geometry defaults are invented; missing geometry blocks.

Capability: Creates and deletes section and material records, and deletes components, blocking deletion of records that other entities still reference.
Assigns a shared section to a pipe element or detaches it, materializing and propagating cached section properties to bound elements on a private candidate model.
Notes: No in-module unit tests; exercised through the public engine and desktop tests.

Capability: Creates and deletes supports and replaces a support configuration, validating restraints, springs, constant and variable hangers and nonlinear settings with explicit dimensioned inputs.
Notes: Blocks deletion of supports with dependent primitive loads; conflicting stiffness declarations are rejected.

Capability: Validates grouped (composite) support boundary-association metadata across a batch, requiring complete model-hash evidence and canonical member mechanics; adds no solver mechanics.
Notes: Read-only metadata; legacy supports without association remain valid.

Capability: Replaces material temperature-point tables and wind-exposure load data as validated atomic rich edits with per-quantity units, bracket checks and partial-row warnings.
Notes: Computes no physics; envelope must be unit none/dimensionless with units carried per quantity.

Capability: Creates and deletes load cases and primitive loads (e.g. concentrated forces) and edits their magnitudes, blocking deletion of load cases used by combinations.
Creates and deletes load combinations of mechanics, result-state subtraction and range-envelope bases, and adds or removes combination terms with factor checks.
Notes: Combination arithmetic is not performed here; only structure and references are validated.

Capability: Splits a pipe run at a point or rigidly transforms pipe runs and their nodes, carrying attachments and metadata with bounded geometry-only edits.
Notes: No desktop or e2e test found that drives split or transform through the UI.

Capability: Validates or applies an ordered batch of operations atomically on a private evolving document; any failure rolls back and returns no model, and submitted validation claims are untrusted.
Notes: Requires complete initial model hash; rejects duplicate ids and empty batches at preflight.

Capability: Converts quantities for display through the unit catalog without altering stored values, returning explicit unavailable entries for unknown units or non-finite results.
Notes: Distinguishes absolute and interval temperatures; rejects pressure-reference payloads.

Capability: Exposes the operation engine, batch engine, display conversion and canonical JSON hashing to the browser as a feature-gated wasm32 build with JSON-string exports and structured input-error envelopes.
Notes: Built only with --features wasm; native builds never compile the module.

Capability: Validates proposed operation sets against an accepted model-state snapshot and produces deterministic preview deltas, blocking direct-mutation requests and unitless quantities.
Notes: Python contract engine; no product-runtime caller found outside tests. Uses the schema dimension vocabulary reader.

Capability: Records deterministic user acceptance or rejection decisions over operations with validation outcomes and diff-preview references, gating acceptance on an explicit user signal.
Notes: Python contract engine; does not apply operations. No product-runtime caller found outside tests.

Capability: Records agent rationale as decision-support metadata bound to operation and audit context, flagging unresolved assumptions and professional-claim wording.
Notes: Python contract engine; never accepts work or mutates model state. No product-runtime caller found outside tests.

Capability: Builds a deterministic accessibility and usability baseline review over GUI surface records (viewport, tree, editors, warnings, results, solve), reporting findings and coverage.
Notes: Python record builder; the desktop accessibility panel names these surfaces as strings but does not execute this module.

Capability: Composes design-knowledge, constraint-warning, state/run browser, comparison tables, graphical overlays and operation diff-review panels into inspectable workspace state.
Notes: Python record builder; the desktop design workspace panel cites this module path as metadata only.

Capability: Builds deterministic material, component and rule-pack-reference editor records with per-field unit metadata and validation state.
Notes: Python contract only; no product-runtime caller found.

Capability: Builds model-tree nodes, selection and property-inspector records for model entities with validation state and privacy classification.
Notes: Python contract only; no product-runtime caller found.

Capability: Builds result-viewer records for displacement, rotation, force, moment, reaction, stress and ratio results with unit metadata, finiteness checks and hash-boundary status.
Notes: Python contract only; no product-runtime caller found.

Capability: Builds a solve-run timeline over queued, running, cancelling, cancelled, completed and failed states, with cancellation summary and pending-terminal-state warning.
Notes: Python contract only; does not run solvers.

Capability: Classifies missing-data, provenance, assumption, solve-required and code-check-required conditions into warning or blocking records mapped to analysis statuses.
Notes: Python contract only; no product-runtime caller found.

Capability: Supplies shared unit, analysis-status, persistence-hash and source-of-truth boundary helpers and diagnostics used by the GUI record builders.
Notes: Keeps its own copy of the canonical dimension list rather than reading the units schema.

Capability: Models in-memory viewport session state and prepares node-creation, pipe-run connection, component-symbol insertion and selection command intents plus view primitives.
Notes: Standalone crate with no dependents found; the desktop viewport implements its own intents. Python test checks schema and fixture shape, not this crate.

Capability: Checks constraint records and design-knowledge references for required fields, provenance, units, assumptions and professional boundary, classifying connectivity, clearance and slope conflicts.
Notes: Decision-support diagnostics only; no product-runtime caller found outside tests.

Capability: Provides the canonical dimension vocabulary, exponent-vector algebra and a closed SI/US unit catalog with SI-canonical units and definitional constants.
Notes: Consumed by the operation engine, product physics, rule-check runner and the desktop backend.

Capability: Converts values between units of the same dimension, with affine absolute-temperature versus interval conversion and gauge/absolute pressure conversion requiring an explicit reference.
Notes: No silent atmospheric default; non-finite and incompatible-dimension inputs are errors.

Capability: Returns the unit catalog to the desktop frontend for unit pickers and display.
Notes: Command lives in the desktop backend; catalog content comes from the units crate.

Capability: Reads the accepted dimension identifiers from the units schema for Python callers, rejecting a missing, malformed or duplicated enum.
Notes: Also referenced by the headless runner.

Capability: Describes the unit core contract: storage convention for quantities, catalog scope, temperature and pressure semantics and what the crate does not wire.
Notes: Some statements describe an earlier phase and say units are not yet wired into application fields, which later code does.

Capability: Records an earlier task run that produced the unit crate, with its scope, tools and outcome.
Notes: Historical run evidence stored inside a code folder; carries an absolute path from another machine.

Capability: Renders JSON as RFC 8785 canonical text (UTF-16 key order, ECMAScript number form) so every hash seam produces identical bytes for identical values.
Notes: Documented divergence: integers beyond 2^53 keep full precision. Used by the operation engine, runner, reporting and rule-pack crates.

Capability: Canonicalizes JSON text under a strict checked profile that rejects duplicate keys and integers or magnitudes outside the I-JSON safe range.
Provides a feature-gated command-line canonicalizer that reads a versioned batch request on stdin and returns canonical text per item, plus a Python subprocess adapter that calls it without fallback.
Notes: Adapter never builds, searches PATH or uses a shell; fails if the binary is absent. Used by analysis-run compatibility and stress-neutral handoff packaging.

Capability: Builds and validates deterministic project persistence envelopes with model, state and run history, hash metadata, provenance, private-data markers and a hash manifest; supports round-trip checks.
Notes: Byte basis is sorted compact JSON, explicitly not RFC 8785.

Capability: Creates, opens, saves, version-checks and migrates a local SQLite project store and rebuilds its retrieval sidecars, with JSON payload bytes kept as the source of truth.
Notes: Python service; the desktop backend has its own separate Rust store, so no product-runtime caller of this module was found.

Capability: Creates and validates references to external artifacts carried in a project envelope, including hash evidence.
Validates parsed material, section and component library imports for required provenance, public redistribution and review status, private-only handling, protected-content quarantine and units.
Notes: Python reference contract; parses no external file formats and makes no legal determinations.

Capability: Validates hanger library imports against the standalone hanger schema: identities, repeated records, provenance and fully dimensioned quantities.
Notes: Python only; no hanger path found in the Rust port.

Capability: Enforces the library import provenance and quarantine rules in the desktop runtime, projecting findings into the import-boundary diagnostic envelope used before a library is stored.
Notes: Rust port of the Python checker; parity pinned by shared invented fixtures.

Capability: Explains the library import provenance checker, its checks and limits, and the hanger library boundary.
Explains the Rust library import validation crate, its relation to the Python contract and its parity testing.
